transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess what finally made me come in is I’ve been hearing my name called. Like from the hallway at home, and I’ll go look and nobody’s there. And then it happened once at the warehouse too, which really shook me up because I know all the little noises there, you know, forklifts beeping and pallets dragging, people yelling across aisles—so I can usually tell what’s what.

But this sounded real. Like someone was right there, like my husband standing next to me saying my name. That scared me.
Have you ever seen anything that wasn't really there, like shadows or figures, when you were hearing your name?

I don’t know about seeing shadows or figures, not really… what scared me was more hearing it. Like my name from the hallway at home, and then that one time at the warehouse—nobody was there, but it sounded real, like my husband was standing right next to me saying it. I kept looking around, you know, and at work there’s already so much noise, but this was different.
Have you been using any alcohol or drugs recently?

Um… recently? I mean, I don’t really know how to answer that exactly. Like, I’ve never been the kind of person who goes out partying or anything. After work I’m usually just so tired, I go home and there’s dinner and laundry and all that. 

Alcohol, maybe if it’s around at a cookout or something, but… I don’t know, recently? Not anything that stands out to me. Drugs, no—unless you mean like over-the-counter stuff? Because sometimes people say “drugs” and I’m like, well, everybody takes something at some point, you know?
Have you heard any other voices or sounds that aren't really there, aside from your name being called?

Mostly it’s just my name. Like… that’s the thing that made me finally come in, because I’d hear it from the hallway at home, and I’d go check, and nobody was there.

And then that time at the warehouse, with all the regular noises going on, it still sounded so clear—like my husband was standing right next to me saying my name. I can’t really say there’s other voices talking or anything like that. It’s just that, but it feels real enough to scare me.
Have you been drinking more alcohol than usual lately?

I don’t think so… I mean, I’m not counting drinks or anything. Sometimes there’s wine or beer around if we’re at someone’s house, but lately I’ve mostly just been going to work and coming home. The warehouse has been exhausting, and by the time I get home I’m thinking about dinner or whether I remembered to switch the laundry over, not really drinking. So… no, I haven’t noticed drinking more than usual.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Yeah… I guess I have. It’s kind of like after all that running around and arguing—like I was just wound up and everything was too much—and then I just sort of dropped. 

I’ll sit at the kitchen table and suddenly I’m crying, and there isn’t even a real reason right then. The table will have mail on it, or a cup from breakfast, and I’m thinking I should get up and wipe it down, but I just… can’t get myself back. It feels heavy and empty.
Do you hear your name being called all the time, or does it happen only sometimes?

Only sometimes. It’s not like every minute or anything… it’ll happen when I’m at home, like from the hallway, and I’ll stop what I’m doing because it sounds so real. I’ll think, “Did he just call me?” and then nobody’s there.

There was that one time at the warehouse too, and I know it’s noisy there with carts and boxes and the beeping, but it still sounded like my husband was right next to me saying my name. That’s what scared me enough to come in.
Do you usually hear your name being called when you're feeling sad or down?

Not really when I’m sad, no. It was more during that stretch where I wasn’t sleeping much and I was talking all the time, like I had to fix everything right then. I was just… going and going.

Before that I don’t remember hearing anything like that, and then once I got low and quiet and kind of pulled into myself, it hasn’t been happening like that. It’s weird, because you’d think feeling bad would be when your mind plays tricks on you, but for me it was when I was all wound up.
Have you ever smelled or tasted something that wasn't really there?

Smelled or tasted? No, I don’t think so… not like that. I mean, sometimes at the warehouse you smell cardboard or that dusty smell from the boxes, and at home the hallway gets this old-house smell, but that’s real, I think.

What scared me was more hearing my name—like from the hallway at home when nobody was there, and that one time at work it sounded just like my husband standing right next to me saying it. That’s the thing I can’t shake.
Have you ever heard a voice telling you to do something?

Not telling me to do something, no… not like instructions. It’s more just my name, which sounds simple, but it really scares me because it feels so real.

Like at home, I’ll hear it from the hallway and I’ll think my husband is calling me, and then there’s nobody there. And that one time at the warehouse—there’s always noise there, boxes and carts and everything—but it sounded like he was right next to me saying my name. That’s what made me think, okay, something’s not right.
Have you ever heard a voice telling you what to do or giving you commands?

No, not commands exactly… I don’t hear it saying, like, “go do this” or “don’t do that.” It’s more my name. That’s what scared me enough to come in.

I’ll be at home and hear my name from the hallway, and I think it’s my husband, so I go look, and nobody’s there. And once at the warehouse, with all the carts and boxes and people moving around, it sounded as real as him standing right next to me saying my name. That one really shook me.
Have you used any alcohol or drugs in the 24 hours before one of these times when you heard your name being called?

I mean… I don’t think so. I’m not really someone who keeps track like that, hour by hour. Sometimes after work I’m so tired I just come home and everything kind of blends together, you know? The warehouse schedule messes with me, and then dinner, laundry, my husband asking where something is…

But no, I can’t think of a time where I was using something right before it happened. I don’t really know if that’s what you mean.
Do you think the hearing of your name could be related to alcohol or drug use?

I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed it being tied to that, but I’m not great at connecting those things. Like, sometimes I’ll have a glass of wine at a family thing or whatever, but the times I’m thinking of, it wasn’t like I was sitting there using anything and then suddenly hearing my name.

It feels more random than that. But I guess I don’t keep a perfect record… I’m usually just trying to get through work and home stuff, and then by the time something happens I’m already upset and not thinking, “what did I do 24 hours ago?”
How long have you been hearing your name being called?

Um… I think it’s been about three weeks? It’s hard to pin down exactly because the days kind of run together with work and home and everything, but this whole thing—being really wound up and restless, then hearing my name, and then kind of crashing after—it’s been going on around three weeks.
Do you think your hearing your name being called could be related to your use of alcohol?

I’m not sure. I mean, I don’t really think of myself as drinking much, but then again my sister will say, “Oh, you had wine at dinner,” and I’m like, okay, but that was with food, you know? Not like… I don’t know.

I haven’t noticed it happening because of alcohol. It’s not like I take a drink and then hear my name. The times I remember, I was just doing regular stuff, and honestly half the time I’m thinking about work schedules or whether I forgot something at the store. So… I don’t know that it’s related.
Have you noticed any difference in how often you hear your name being called when you've been drinking versus when you haven't?

I haven’t really noticed a difference, no. I mean, the thing that scared me enough to come in wasn’t like, “Oh, I drank and then it happened.” It was hearing my name from the hallway at home when nobody was there, and once at the warehouse too—like I was sure somebody was calling me.

And it sounds real, that’s the part that gets me. Like my husband could be standing right next to me saying it. But whether I had been drinking or not… I can’t say I’ve seen a pattern.
Have you noticed any difference in your hearing of your name when you haven't been using any alcohol or drugs at all?

Yeah… I mean, I haven’t been using drugs, and with alcohol, I don’t think it lines up. Like, what scared me enough to come in was hearing my name from the hallway at home when nobody was there. And then once at the warehouse too, which is embarrassing because I turned like someone had called me, and nobody had.

It sounds real, that’s the thing. Not like a thought in my head—more like my husband standing right next to me saying it. And then I start wondering if I missed something, like did someone come in, did I leave the TV on, and then I’m checking the hallway… sorry, I know that’s not exactly what you asked. But no, I haven’t noticed it only happening when I’ve had alcohol or anything.
Do you think your hearing your name being called happens more often when you have been drinking alcohol?

I don’t think it’s more when I’ve been drinking, no. What scared me enough to come in is that I’ve been hearing my name called from the hallway at home, and once at the warehouse too, when nobody was there.

It’s not like a fuzzy thing either—it sounds real, like my husband is standing right next to me saying my name. And then I’ll stop what I’m doing and look around, and… I mean, at the warehouse I felt stupid because I turned like someone needed me. But I can’t say alcohol makes it happen more.
Do you think your hearing your name being called would stop if you completely stopped drinking alcohol?

I don’t know that stopping drinking would make it stop, honestly. I mean, maybe I’d be willing to try if you think it matters, but the thing that scared me wasn’t tied to that in my mind.

It’s like… I’ll be at home and hear my name from the hallway when nobody’s there. And once it happened at the warehouse, which was awful because I turned around like someone had called me. It sounds real—like my husband standing right next to me saying my name. So I can’t really say, “Oh, if I stopped drinking, it would go away.” I just don’t know.
Do you think your hearing of your name would go away if you stopped using any substances, including alcohol, completely?

I don’t really think I can say it would go away just from stopping everything. I mean, I haven’t connected it to that. What scared me enough to come in was hearing my name from the hallway at home when nobody was there, and then it happened once at the warehouse too.

And it’s not like… you know when you think you hear something because a machine makes a weird noise or the fridge clicks? It wasn’t like that. It sounded real, like my husband was standing right next to me saying my name. So I don’t know if stopping alcohol completely would change it. I just know it felt real and it scared me.

patient.answer:
I don’t really think I can say it would go away just from stopping everything. I mean, I haven’t connected it to that. What scared me enough to come in was hearing my name from the hallway at home when nobody was there, and then it happened once at the warehouse too.

And it’s not like… you know when you think you hear something because a machine makes a weird noise or the fridge clicks? It wasn’t like that. It sounded real, like my husband was standing right next to me saying my name. So I don’t know if stopping alcohol completely would change it. I just know it felt real and it scared me.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports hearing their name being called when no one is around, which is a hallucination. The patient denies substance-induced psychosis and there's no clear evidence that substance use is the cause of the hallucinations. The presence of hallucinations without a clear substance-induced cause, along with the patient's report of feeling sad or down, suggests a diagnosis of acute and transient psychotic disorder (F23).
